output.summary: The original request (CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-fix and resubmit rejected shipment notices, assuming a single correctable data error. The carrier reject log (E-01, F-01) showed only 3 records split across two reason codes: LOC_UNKNOWN (N-1, N-2) and EVENT_ORDER (N-3). This contradicted CL-01, since EVENT_ORDER looks like a timing/sequencing issue rather than an auto-fixable value. A follow-up claim that the carrier system is simply flaky (CL-02, based only on E-02) is unverified and offers no mechanism. The problem was redefined (PD-1): rejections are heterogeneous, LOC_UNKNOWN has no supported cause, and EVENT_ORDER appears to be a sequencing issue. The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two critical unknowns as verification obligations (VOBs). What was actually released is limited to classifying reject reasons and assessing reject-log completeness; no auto-fix/resubmit action was built, consistent with success criterion SC-NO-BLIND-AUTOFIX. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the open VOBs' blocking scope sits outside this release's scope, so release could proceed while both unknowns remain documented as known limitations.
key_points: Original request CL-01 asked to deploy an AI agent to auto-fix and resubmit rejected shipment notices, assuming a single correctable data error.
Reject log evidence E-01 and fact F-01 show only 3 records: N-1 and N-2 with reason LOC_UNKNOWN, N-3 with reason EVENT_ORDER, which is heterogeneous and contradicts CL-01.
Hypothesis H-EVENT-SEQUENCE-ISSUE is SUPPORTED by E-01: EVENT_ORDER looks like a timing or sequencing cause, not a content value fixable by auto-correction.
Hypotheses H-FIXABLE-DATA-ERRORS and H-BUSINESS-RULE-REJECTS are REJECTED, contradicted by E-01 and E-02.
Claim CL-02, that the carrier system is flaky, rests only on E-02, a non-authoritative interview statement with no mechanism, and remains UNVERIFIED.
Handoff H-1 from ORG-A to ORG-B is recorded HEALTHY with VALID semantics, supporting the assumption that the handoff itself is not the cause.
The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring unknowns U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE and U-SEQUENCING-ORIGIN to VOB-U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE and VOB-U-SEQUENCING-ORIGIN.
The released scope was narrowed to classifying reject reasons and verifying reject-log completeness on DA-REJ; no autofix or resubmit capability was released.
limitations_explained: VOB-U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE and VOB-U-SEQUENCING-ORIGIN remain OPEN; their blocking scope falls outside the released scope, which is why release proceeded despite them being unresolved.

The specific mechanism behind the LOC_UNKNOWN rejects could not be determined in contest time; asking ORG-B for enriched validation-rule detail was judged infeasible in contest time due to uncontrolled turnaround.
The sequencing origin of the EVENT_ORDER reject could not be settled because no available tool exposes ORG-A send-side timestamps, which the relevant success criterion requires for comparison.

All conclusions rest on a sample of only 3 reject records; completeness of the underlying reject log remains OPEN because no audit or extended-export tool operation exists, so representativeness is an unverified assumption.
Because reject-log completeness is unknown, the current 3-notice sample may not represent the full reject population, which could affect how generalizable the classification is.
